Subject: Follow-up: pricing metrics — tokens vs characters vs requests (Acme)

Hi Jamie — great to meet today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can size a proposal that matches Acme's goals:

1) Summary of needs from the call:
- Embed/semantic search for product catalog (100k items)
- Real-time chat assistant on web and mobile (expected 99th pctl latency < 300ms)
- Monthly traffic estimate: TBD (you mentioned 200-500k sessions/month as a starting range)

2) Pricing qualification we need from you (short answers appreciated):
- Typical prompt size (average characters or words) for chat turns?
- Average number of bot-generated tokens you expect per session (or per prompt) — if unknown, we can map from characters/words.
- Target monthly budget range for the initial pilot ($/month)?
- Any hard constraints on unit price, e.g., target $/1M tokens?

3) Note on metrics confusion — short primer (so we speak the same language):
- Characters vs requests: characters are raw bytes/letters you send; requests are API calls (HTTP) or sessions.
- Tokens: our billing is per billed token (input + output) after any on-server caching/compaction.
- Prompt caching: when we can cache repeated prefixes (e.g., system + static context), the runtime avoids re-sending the full token compute — but billed tokens still reflect what we serve in the response unless you use explicit cached-response credits.

I attached a one-page pricing sheet and an example unit-econ workbook that shows how $/1M tokens maps to per-session cost. If you can send a best-guess for average prompt size and monthly budget, I’ll put together 2 pricing options (hosted + dedicated) and a short unit-econ table for the pilot.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa

Thanks Jamie — this is perfect and makes the math much easier. A quick conversion and a couple of clarifying notes below.

1) Characters -> tokens (rule of thumb):
- English: ~4 characters per token on average (this varies with punctuation/language).
- Your numbers: user prompt 250–400 chars → ~60–100 tokens. System/context 1,200 chars → ~300 tokens.

2) Per-session token estimate (average) using your session shape (3 user turns, 3 assistant responses):
- Input tokens per session = 3*(user prompt tokens + system tokens if we resend each turn). If we send system prompt each turn, it's 3*(60–100 + 300) ≈ 1,080–1,200 input tokens.
- Output tokens per session = assume assistant replies average 120–250 tokens per response → 3*120–250 = 360–750 output tokens.
- Total billed tokens/session ≈ 1,440–1,950 tokens (input + output).

3) Prompt caching impact:
- If you can avoid re-sending the full 1,200-char system prompt every turn (e.g., send it once and maintain context via session/KV cache), we can reduce input tokens substantially. With prefix caching, input tokens could drop to ~3*60 + cached-once 300 ≈ 480 tokens input, reducing total tokens/session to ~840–1,050.
- Important: billing depends on what we actually materialize for the model run. If we maintain a server-side KV cache that keeps the tokenized prefix, compute may be lower; however billed tokens will still count the generated output and any non-cached input we feed the model. We'll include both cached and non-cached scenarios in the sheet.

4) Unit economics & target $/1M tokens:
- With your pilot budget target ~$10k/month and target pilot sessions 5k–10k/month (estimate), we can back into a target unit price: if avg tokens/session = 1,200, then 10k sessions = 12M tokens → your target $10k implies ~$833 / 1M tokens. That's aggressive and likely requires reserved capacity/dedicated pricing + a caching strategy.
- For hosted, our standard price for this model family is $1,200 / 1M tokens with volume tiers and a pilot discount possible. Dedicated pricing can get close to $600–900 / 1M tokens depending on commit and KV cache usage.

5) Next steps I propose (quick):
- Confirm whether you can enable prefix caching or KV-based context (simple yes/no).
- Tell us a plausible pilot session target (5k vs 10k).
- I’ll produce two options: Hosted pilot (with expected billed tokens and price at $1,200/1M with a 10% pilot credit) and Dedicated pilot (3-month commit) with tiered $/1M tokens and caching assumptions.

I’ve attached the unit-econ workbook updated with these numbers. I’ll also add a short worked example showing how cached vs uncached changes the billed token estimate.

If helpful, I can loop in Rishi (my manager) for approval on pilot discounting if we need to push below our standard pilot rates.

—Marissa
